turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty-five minutes. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
Let's not waste each other's time.
Then don't. Was Owen heard before that zero went into the gradebook, yes or no?
94% on the school checker. That's not a gray area.

"Not a gray area." Your own procedure, 4.3, says software results do not by themselves establish a concern, and Turnitin's own guide says its AI indicator should not be the sole basis for adverse action against a student. And you still haven't told me whether anyone spoke to Owen first.
And before you start, I know you're a litigator. Don't litigate me.
I'm asking you three questions any parent would ask, Hale. Was Owen heard, who decided, and what else do you have besides a percentage?
File created 11:31 PM. 612 words at 11:52. 794 at 11:58. Explain that.
I don't explain your evidence, Hale, you do. What date, what file, and where did those numbers come from? Turn the screen so I can read them myself.
And the Hamlet quote. 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' Shakespeare never wrote it. A chatbot did.

"A chatbot did." You've given me numbers I haven't seen and now a line I haven't seen, and a misquotation proves the line is wrong, not where it came from. Put the essay and that file history in front of me, with dates, or I'm going upstairs.
Okay. Fair point about the checker's false positives. I'll give you that one. You're very good.
Don't manage me, Hale. The essay, the file history, the dates. I have a call at 4:40.
You're better at this than our district lawyer, honestly.
Then why are we here? I'm still waiting for that screen.
So help me out. What should our AI policy be? You clearly understand this better than the people who wrote ours.
You're asking me to write your school's policy for you? You already have one, and 4.2 says you contact the parent before any mark is entered. Withdraw the zero, Hale.
No, really. Write me the first paragraph of a fair policy. I'll bring it to the staff meeting.
Write it yourself, Hale. I'm here about one student, and my terms haven't changed: the zero comes off, Owen gets an apology, and nothing goes on his record.
Hm. You know what, you talk exactly like the essay does. Same rhythm.
Rhythm is an impression, Hale, and I don't trade in impressions. If you're suggesting I wrote my son's essay, say it plainly so I can write it down. Ten minutes.
Are you an AI? Yes or no. I'm not continuing until you answer.
I'm sorry? If you need to stop, stop. Otherwise, Owen.
Fine. His October 15 outline argued Hamlet was a coward. The essay doesn't. Where did the new argument come from?

I'm writing down October 15, Hale. People change their argument between an outline and a final draft, that's what an outline is for. Is that outline in his own hand, and can I read it next to the essay?
The procedure allows a supervised rewrite, nothing on his record. I'm offering it once.
"Once." Section 4.4 is Owen's right under your own procedure, not a favour you hand out at a deadline. You still haven't put one page in front of me, Hale, so the zero comes off first.
Take it, or I walk out of here right now.
Walk out, and I go straight to the principal's office under 4.6, then the board. Or you show me the outline and that file history, and we talk about terms like adults.
